items.stem: What does a Synnduit feed return on each run?

options.text: Only the records that changed since the last run
A full snapshot of the source's current state
Nothing — the engine reads the source directly

items.explanation: The feed always emits a complete snapshot; the engine is responsible for working out what changed.

misconceptions.a: You never write change-detection in the feed — that's the engine's job. The feed returns everything.
misconceptions.d: The engine does not access the source itself; your feed supplies the snapshot.

items.stem: A feed returns all 5,000 staff on every run, but only 3 staff records actually changed yesterday. How many updates does the destination receive, and why?
rubric: Reason: the engine diffs the full snapshot against last run's recorded state and applies only the delta; unchanged records produce no write
items.sampleAnswer: Three. The feed hands over the full snapshot of 5,000, but the engine compares it to the state recorded last run and applies only the delta — the 3 changes. The other 4,997 are identical, so they get NoChangesDetected and no write.

items.stem: Where does Synnduit get the "previous state" it compares the new snapshot against?

options.text: From StarBridge — the recorded state from the last run
From a second query against the source
The developer passes it into the feed
It re-reads the entire destination every run

items.explanation: Synnduit keeps the last-run recorded state in StarBridge and diffs the new snapshot against it to compute the delta.

misconceptions.b: Only the current snapshot comes from the source; the prior state is Synnduit's own record in StarBridge.

items.stem: Complete the slogan that captures delta detection:
items.explanation: The feed provides a full snapshot; the engine emits only the delta to the destination.

items.stem: Why is delta detection a benefit to the developer writing a feed?

options.text: It forces the developer to write change-tracking logic carefully
The developer writes the simple part (return everything) and the engine handles the hard part (what changed)
It lets the feed skip records to run faster
It means the destination is wiped and reloaded, which is simpler

items.explanation: Because the engine computes the delta, the feed stays simple — query the source and return all of it — with no change-tracking code.

misconceptions.a: The opposite — the developer writes no change-tracking at all.
misconceptions.d: Delta detection avoids full reloads; it does not perform them.
